<issue identifier="MM-475">
<title>did:web sovereign sessions and wallet-confirmed OAuth consent</title>
<description>
## Summary

Both passwordless auth paths are hard-gated to `did:plc`, so a `did:web` account has no way to authenticate at all when it carries no password — which every wallet-migrated account does, since the migration `createAccount` request has no `password` field and the server stores NULL for it by design.

* `POST /v1/sessions/sovereign` — `is_plc_did` gate (`routes/sovereign_session.rs`)
* `POST /oauth/authorize/approve` — same gate (`routes/oauth_consent.rs`)
* the password consent form folds NULL into `VerifyResult::WrongPassword` (`routes/oauth_authorize.rs`)

## Why this is more than a login inconvenience

`SessionProvider::full_access_client` is the seam every authenticated wallet operation on a Custos-hosted identity goes through, and its ladder ends at `NeedsUnlock` → biometric sovereign login. `restore_blob_backup` sits on that seam and has its own `SessionExpired` variant that tells the frontend to run exactly that login.

So for a passwordless `did:web` account, **the wallet's own iCloud media restore is reachable only while the refresh chain from migration survives.** Once it lapses, sovereign login 401s on the `is_plc_did` gate and the recovery path is gone. This was on the critical path during the <issue id="6a22b24b-7904-49cc-b5dd-e4d5386b8b54" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-472/blob-gc-destroys-the-blobs-of-any-account-whose-reconcile-fails">MM-472</issue> recovery.

## The change is one lookup

Signature verification is already method-agnostic — `crypto::verify_did_key_signature` on a `did:key:` URI, accepting P-256 and secp256k1. The only PLC-specific step is the authority lookup:

```rust
let plc = fetch_current_plc_state(...).await?;
if !plc.rotation_keys.iter().any(|key| key == &request.signing_key) { ... }
```

The did:web counterpart primitive already exists: `identity::resolution::resolve_web_did_document` does a live, SSRF-guarded, cache-bypassing HTTPS fetch — the structural mirror of `fetch_current_plc_state`.

The wallet side needs nothing. `sovereign_login_impl` never inspects the DID method.

## Decided policy

**Authority set is exactly** `{did}#device`**, and nothing else.** Not "any verificationMethod": `#atproto`'s private key is Custos-held, so a broader set would let this server sign its own sovereign-session envelope for an account it hosts. `create_did.rs` already enforces `#device` specifically when promoting a new did:web, so this keeps one rule across both paths.

**Match** `create_did.rs`**'s predicate** — `type == "Multikey"`, `controller == did`, exact `{did}#device` id. Difference in shape: `has_key` *verifies* a known key by comparing `publicKeyMultibase`; the authority lookup *discovers* it, so it extracts that field instead. Note the VM carries bare multibase while PLC stores `did:key:` URIs — render `format!("did:key:{}", multibase)` before comparing.

**Reject a document with multiple** `#device`**-shaped entries as malformed.** Duplicate `id` values already violate DID Core. Fail closed.

**Resolve live, never from cache.** The `did_documents` cache is writable by `POST /v1/did-web/document`.

**Gate on self-hosted only, server-side.** `POST /v1/did-web/document` lets an account rewrite its served document under session auth, so for a Custos-hosted did:web a stolen session could install an attacker `#device` key and bootstrap sovereign sessions — a privilege escalation with no key compromise. did:plc has no equivalent hole (rewriting the rotation set needs an existing rotation key, and [plc.directory](<http://plc.directory>) is external).

The gate is exact rather than approximate: `POST /v1/did-web/document` already refuses unless hosting is enabled (`routes/did_web_hosting.rs`), so `did_web_hosting_enabled_at IS NULL` **is** the condition "no session-authed rewrite is possible", with no gap in either direction.

Enforcement must be server-side in the authority lookup. Hiding the Custos-hosted shapes in the wallet is a sensible default but is not a security boundary — `enable_managed_hosting` is already a plumbed parameter on both wallet flows, and the route stays live for any other client and for accounts that already opted in.

## Scope

1. New `crates/pds/src/identity/authority.rs` — `authorized_signing_keys(state, did)`, dispatching did:plc → existing `fetch_current_plc_state` path, did:web → `resolve_web_did_document` + the `#device` policy + hosting gate. Lives in `identity/` because routes may not import one another.
2. Delete the `is_plc_did` gates in `sovereign_session.rs` and `oauth_consent.rs`; both switch to the shared lookup. Their existing `rejected()` / `approval_rejected()` helpers already collapse every failure to one opaque message, so no new enumeration surface.
3. Wallet: stop offering the two Custos-hosted did:web shapes (of the four in ADR-0022), deferring them until the document-rewrite circularity is resolved.
4. ADR-0022 amendment recording the `#device`-only policy, the hosting gate and why it is exact, and the deferral.
5. Changelog fragment — both routes are shipped surfaces.

## Later upgrade path

Making `#device` immutable across a `/v1/did-web/document` edit would let the hosting gate be dropped and all four ADR-0022 shapes supported, without redesigning anything.

## Interim

Keep a password set on `did:web:malpercio.dev` until this ships, purely as a second key to the door.

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

8	## Context
9	
10	ADR-0003 made `did:plc` the only account identity method because its ordered rotation keys and
11	72-hour recovery window support client-held custody. That remains the strongest default, but it
12	also excluded identities whose root of trust is intentionally a user-owned domain. Custos can
13	support those identities without claiming that domain control has PLC's recovery semantics.
14	
15	Serving a DID for a domain the user does not control would create indefinite exit liability. A
16	new or migrated `did:web` therefore needs an external proof that the wallet-approved document is
17	already authoritative at the user's domain before Custos creates the account or takes over hosting.
18	
19	## Decision
20	
21	Custos may mint, migrate, or host a `did:web` identity only for a user-owned domain, after the
22	wallet proves control by publishing the exact reviewed DID document at its authoritative HTTPS
23	URL. `did:plc` remains the default identity method.
24	
25	The document publishes the wallet device key alongside Custos's reserved `#atproto` key and
26	`#atproto_pds` service. The existing 2-of-3 escrow restores the device key, not domain ownership.
27	Custos-hosted updates require device-key approval; self-hosted identities use that key as a
28	monitoring anchor. DNS remains the immediate override and exit boundary.
29	
30	Wallet recovery language and controls are method-specific. PLC monitoring, fork-point recovery,
31	and the 72-hour override apply only to `did:plc`; `did:web` recovery is domain control plus
32	escrowed keys.
33	
34	## Consequences
35	
36	- Users can create or migrate all four new/existing and self/Custos-hosted `did:web` shapes.
37	- Account promotion performs an SSRF-hardened external fetch and exact byte comparison; it never
38	  submits a PLC operation.
39	- Domain compromise remains identity compromise. Device-key escrow restores co-signing and
40	  monitoring continuity but cannot replace domain control.
41	- Custos accepts hosting liability only after independently observable proof of user control, and
42	  users can exit by repointing DNS.
43	- Method-specific UI and recovery paths must remain gated so `did:web` never inherits PLC claims.
44	
45	## Alternatives considered
46	
47	- **Keep `did:plc` as the only method.** Rejected because it prevents users from choosing domain
48	  control as their identity root and blocks migration of existing `did:web` accounts.
49	- **Mint `did:web` before publication.** Rejected because an authenticated wallet session does not
50	  prove control of the named domain.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The `is_plc_did` gate exists in *two* route files as a duplicated private fn — a symptom that the real abstraction (an authority lookup) was missing. Because this codebase forbids route→route imports, the fix has to land in `identity/`, which is exactly where the issue puts it.

input.new_string:
## Amendment (2026-07-25): signing authority for passwordless auth

Both passwordless auth surfaces — `POST /v1/sessions/sovereign` and `POST /oauth/authorize/approve`
— were hard-gated to `did:plc`, so a `did:web` account carrying no password (which every
wallet-migrated account does, by design) could not authenticate at all. Extending them to `did:web`
requires deciding what counts as that identity's signing authority.

**The authority set is exactly `{did}#device`, and nothing else.** Not "any verificationMethod":
`#atproto`'s private key is Custos-held, so a broader set would let this server sign its own
sovereign-session envelope for an account it hosts. This keeps one rule across both `did:web` paths
— account promotion already enforces `#device` specifically. The predicate matches promotion's
(`type == "Multikey"`, `controller == did`, exact `{did}#device` id), differing only in shape: the
authority lookup *discovers* the key by extracting `publicKeyMultibase`, rendered as
`did:key:{multibase}` since a PLC rotation set stores `did:key:` URIs. A document with more than one
`#device`-shaped entry is malformed (duplicate `id` values already violate DID Core) and fails
closed rather than picking one by array order. The document is resolved live; the `did_documents`
cache is never consulted, because `POST /v1/did-web/document` can write it.

**Passwordless auth is gated to self-hosted `did:web` only, enforced server-side.** That same route
lets an account rewrite its served document under mere session auth, so for a Custos-hosted
`did:web` a stolen session could install an attacker `#device` key and bootstrap sovereign sessions
— a privilege escalation with no key compromise. `did:plc` has no equivalent hole: rewriting the
rotation set requires an existing rotation key, and plc.directory is external to this server.

The gate is **exact rather than approximate**: `POST /v1/did-web/document` already refuses unless
hosting is enabled, so `did_web_hosting_enabled_at IS NULL` *is* the condition "no session-authed
rewrite is possible", with no gap in either direction. Enforcement lives in the shared authority
lookup, not the client — the route stays live for any other client and for accounts that already
opted in, so hiding the shapes in the wallet is a sensible default but never the boundary.

Consequently the two **Custos-hosted** `did:web` shapes are **deferred** and no longer offered by
the wallet; the two self-hosted shapes are unaffected, and the hosting routes and their plumbing
remain in place. Making `#device` immutable across a `/v1/did-web/document` edit would let the gate
be dropped and all four shapes supported, without redesigning anything.

## Consequences

- Users can create or migrate the two self-hosted `did:web` shapes. The two Custos-hosted shapes are
  deferred by the amendment above and are not offered.

did:web sovereign sessions and wallet-confirmed OAuth consent (MM-475)

Both passwordless auth paths were hard-gated to did:plc, so a did:web
account carrying no password — which every wallet-migrated account does,
since the migration createAccount request has no password field and the
server stores NULL by design — could not authenticate at all. That was
more than a login inconvenience: SessionProvider::full_access_client is
the seam every authenticated wallet operation goes through, and its
ladder ends at biometric sovereign login, so the wallet's own iCloud
media restore was reachable only while the refresh chain from migration
survived.

Signature verification was already method-agnostic; the only PLC-specific
step was the authority lookup. New identity/authority.rs dispatches on
DID method — did:plc to the existing current-rotation-set fetch, did:web
to a live SSRF-guarded document resolution — and both routes drop their
duplicated is_plc_did gate for it. It lives in identity/ because routes
may not import one another. Their existing rejected()/approval_rejected()
helpers already collapse every failure to one opaque message, so no new
enumeration surface appears.

The did:web authority set is exactly {did}#device and nothing else:
#atproto's private key is Custos-held, so a broader set would let this
server sign its own sovereign envelope for an account it hosts. The
predicate matches create_did.rs's, differing only in that it discovers
the key rather than verifying a known one. A document with multiple
#device-shaped entries is malformed and fails closed.

Passwordless auth is gated to self-hosted did:web, server-side.
POST /v1/did-web/document lets an account rewrite its served document
under session auth, so a stolen session on a Custos-hosted did:web could
install an attacker #device key and bootstrap sovereign sessions —
escalation with no key compromise. That route already refuses unless
hosting is enabled, so did_web_hosting_enabled_at IS NULL *is* the
condition "no session-authed rewrite is possible", exact in both
directions. did:plc has no equivalent hole.

The wallet accordingly stops offering the two Custos-hosted shapes of
ADR-0022's four. The hosting routes and the enable_managed_hosting
plumbing stay in place — hiding shapes in a client is a default, never
the boundary — so lifting the deferral is a UI change.
